preview.headline: Toronto starts on top, and it is not close
preview.dek: The auction is over, nobody has played a game, and we already have opinions. Here is how the ten teams stack up before opening night.

teams.text: Toronto treated the auction like a grocery run with somebody else's card. Luka Dončić cost $25M, and the Jays still walked out with Scottie Barnes, Cade Cunningham and Karl-Anthony Towns. Every starter is signed through at least 2030. The bench has Tyrese Haliburton, Donovan Mitchell and a 39-year-old Kevin Durant on $4M, which is unfair. The only open question is who gets the ball, and that is a lovely question to have.

The Gooners signed Nikola Jokić and Alperen Şengün, two centers who both want the ball at the elbow, and decided to sort it out later. Anthony Edwards and Tyrese Maxey supply the scoring, Giannis Antetokounmpo arrived for $6M, and the whole starting five cost $48M. The other $37M bought a bench that is mostly promise: three guards aged 21 or younger. If the kids hold up, this is the one team that can take a series off Toronto.

Cambridge led the auction for most of the weekend, then watched Dončić and Jokić get bid away on the final day. What is left is still good: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander at $21M, Jayson Tatum, Jalen Brunson and Chet Holmgren, plus Stephen Curry, who is 39 and costs $5M. The Platypuses finished with $29M unspent, the most in the league, which is either discipline or a missed bid depending on who you ask. A playoff team with a guard for every occasion.

Waltham spent a third of its budget on one player, and it is hard to argue. Victor Wembanyama's $33M is the richest deal in the league by $8M. The Bears then signed Josh Giddey for $1M five seconds before the deadline, the best piece of business all weekend. Cooper Flagg, Amen Thompson and Jalen Johnson make this the most athletic frontcourt going. Whether a 23-year-old center and a 21-year-old forward can drag a team into the top four is the season's best subplot.

The Stingrays have Evan Mobley, Bam Adebayo and Jaren Jackson Jr., so good luck scoring at the rim. Scoring at the other end is the worry: the offence runs through Kawhi Leonard, who is 36, and Quentin Grimes. Stony Brook is the best bet among the bottom six to crash the top four, mostly because somebody has to be. Expect a lot of games that finish 98-94.

Durham's starting small forward is LeBron James, who is 43. He is on a one-year deal, which feels right. The actual plan is on the wings, where Trey Murphy III and Deni Avdija cost $13M each, and at point guard, where Ja Morant and a 37-year-old Damian Lillard will take turns. Cameron Boozer, 20, is the rookie to watch. There are 23 years between the oldest and youngest Destroyers, and you may well see both on the floor at once.

The oldest roster in the league already has its first casualty: Jimmy Butler, 38, will miss 35 of the 36 games. The Thunder's richest contract belongs to VJ Edgecombe, who is 22 and makes $12M, twice what Devin Booker does. James Harden is also 38 and also here. There is real talent in Booker, Zion Williamson and Domantas Sabonis, and a real chance most of it is on the injury report by Game 10.

Nashville's second-biggest contract, Moses Moody at $9M, is out for 35 games, so the Elephants open the season with $9M sitting in a suit. What remains is guards: Jalen Suggs, Jamal Murray, Tyler Herro, Immanuel Quickley and Luguentz Dort, all of whom would like the same minutes. Rudy Gobert, 35, and Myles Turner guard the rim. It is a perfectly professional team with no obvious way to win a shootout.

Franz Wagner at $18M is the fourth-richest deal in the league, and the Dragons will need every dollar of it. Anthony Davis is 34 and on a one-year contract, and Pascal Siakam and Fred VanVleet are both 33. Trae Young comes off the bench for $5M, behind a starting five with no point guard in it. Jalen Williams is the piece worth watching. Everything else here has a best-before date.

Somebody has to be last. Queens has Austin Reaves on $13M, De'Aaron Fox, Derrick White and Brandon Ingram, which reads like a decent team until you notice that everyone above them has a star and the Pigeons have four second options. Neemias Queta and Sandro Mamukelashvili are the centers at $6M each. The upside: Stephon Castle is 23 and signed through 2031, and the first pick in the 2027 draft is very much in play.

1.headline: Last-ranked Queens flattens Stony Brook on opening night
1.dek: Austin Reaves scored 38, Jayson Tatum missed three shots all night, and Toronto won by 34 as the favourites and one very loud underdog opened 1-0.

games.text: The preseason rankings had Queens tenth out of ten. Austin Reaves read them. He took 26 shots, 18 of them 3-pointers, made seven and finished with 38 points and eight assists as the Pigeons flattened Stony Brook 128-103. Queens scored 46 in the second quarter and led by 34. Tobias Harris made all five of his shots, four from deep, then strained his groin. Kawhi Leonard went 1-for-8 from three for the Stingrays, who open as the 9 seed. Queens is the 2 seed, which nobody had on the card.

Jayson Tatum took 16 shots and made 13. He took eight 3-pointers and made seven. He finished with 38 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists, and Cambridge buried Rochester 143-123 after leading 79-58 at halftime. Stephen Curry, who is 39, added 24. Rochester's leading scorer was Trae Young, off the bench, with 16 points and nine assists, and Franz Wagner left with a strained hamstring. The Platypuses are the 4 seed. The Dragons are the 7 seed and already short a star.

Toronto was the heavy favourite and behaved like it. Cade Cunningham scored 35, Luka Dončić had 25 with seven rebounds and six assists, Karl-Anthony Towns went 8-for-11 for 20 points and 12 rebounds, and the Jays ran Ithaca off its own floor, 145-111. It was 69-62 at halftime. Then Toronto won the third quarter 36-22 and the game stopped being one. Ithaca got exactly 19 points from three different players, which is tidy and not enough. The Jays are the 1 seed. The Thunder are the 10 seed.

The two-center experiment survived its first night. Nikola Jokić made 12 of 16 shots for 31 points, nine rebounds and eight assists, Anthony Edwards missed once in nine tries for 24, and the Gooners beat Waltham 142-121. The Bears trailed by only five after three quarters, then lost the fourth 35-19. Victor Wembanyama scored 26 but went 3-for-11 from deep. Josh Giddey, the $1M signing, made seven of his eight shots. The Gooners are the 3 seed. Waltham opens as the 8 seed.

LeBron James is 43 and needed 20 shots to score 24, and Durham won anyway, 121-109 at Nashville. Damian Lillard, 37, scored 26 on 12 shots, and Trey Murphy III added 20. The bill arrived late: Ja Morant fractured his nose and will miss the next three games. Nashville got 24 points and nine assists from Jamal Murray and 7-for-20 shooting from Tyler Herro, and trailed by 19 at one point. Durham is the 5 seed, a tiebreak out of the top four. Nashville is the 6 seed.
